hypotheses.reasoning: The POST /v1/notify 503s originate in template-svc. Starting at 18:49:12Z, every call to the third-party email provider api.mailer.example/v3/send returned 503 Bad Gateway or 502 (lines 1623, 1630, 1665, 1693). Before that, template-svc logged only normal renders and GC, so this is the first anomaly on the notify path. The provider failures opened template-svc's circuit breaker (1721), and half-open probes kept failing (1981, 2244). notification-svc then failed renders with 'template-svc returned 503 (circuit open)', and the gateway returned 503 on /v1/notify. The provider fails fast with errors rather than hanging, which points to an external outage rather than a dependency timeout. The provider's status page was not checked, so that is a gap.

A separate, earlier fault is in the login path. Starting around 18:46:54Z, auth-svc calls to the identity provider idp.example/oauth2/token were slow (1398, 1441), then timed out after 30s (1512, 1578). That exhausted account-svc's connection pool to auth-svc (1675, 1831) and produced checkout timeouts (1850). edge-proxy POST /login 503s followed (1731, 1821). This is a real incident, but it affects login rather than /v1/notify, so it is probably not the cause of the notify alert.

verdict.recommendedAction: Confirm the api.mailer.example incident with the provider and fail over to a secondary email provider or queue sends for retry. Keep the template-svc circuit breaker, and make sure notif-worker backs off instead of dropping work while the provider is down. Do not restart template-svc or notification-svc, since the fault is upstream. Separately, investigate idp.example latency for the login path (auth-svc / account-svc pool saturation), which is a second, lower-impact incident.
